summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and a history of two kidney transplants was admitted for acute nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea lasting one day, accompanied by low-grade fever and orthostatic hypotension. She reported sick contacts—her young son and husband—developing similar symptoms. Initial evaluation revealed volume depletion, but no signs of bacterial infection, C. difficile, or influenza. CMV viral load was not detected. She was managed with IV fluids, continued immunosuppressive therapy, and symptom control with Zofran. Her condition improved rapidly, with resolution of vomiting and fever, and she began tolerating oral intake. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue all baseline medications, adjusted atenolol dose, and follow up on pending culture and viral load results.
